items.title: 8.4 Polarized light by the method of reflection

source_refs.note: Topic 8.4 with Fig. 8.6 and Example 8.1 (PDF 177-178, printed 174-175). 'Brewester' is a print misspelling of Brewster.

blocks.text: In 1808 Malus discovered that polarized light is obtained when ordinary light is reflected (light bouncing back from a surface) by a plane sheet of glass. If the reflected light is viewed through a polaroid which is slowly rotated about the line of vision, the light is practically extinguished at one position of the polaroid. The most suitable angle of incidence i is about 57 degrees for glass, for which the reflected ray becomes plane polarized, as illustrated by the ray diagram in Fig. 8.6. This proves that the light reflected by the glass is practically plane polarized. Light reflected from the surface of a table becomes darker when viewed through a rotated polaroid, showing that it is partially plane polarized.

blocks.title: Polarizing angle
blocks.text: The particular angle of incidence on a transparent medium at which the reflected light is almost plane polarized is called the polarizing angle, theta_p.

Let a beam of unpolarized light be made incident on the surface of medium 2 (Fig. 8.6). If the reflected beam of light is almost plane polarized, the reflected and refracted beams are at right angles to each other at the polarizing angle, i = theta_p. Thus theta_p + theta_r = 90 degrees, or theta_r = 90 degrees - theta_p. From Snell's law, n1 sin theta_p = n2 sin theta_r = n2 sin(90 degrees - theta_p) = n2 cos theta_p, so sin theta_p / cos theta_p = n2/n1, that is tan theta_p = n2/n1.

blocks.title: Brewster's law
blocks.text: tan theta_p = n2/n1, where n1 is the refractive index of medium 1 and n2 that of medium 2. If medium 1 is air, n1 = 1 and n2 = n, so tan theta_p = n, where n is the refractive index of the medium on which the light is incident. Hence Brewster proved that the tangent of the angle of polarization is numerically equal to the refractive index of medium 2 when medium 1 is air. In Brewster's law the angle theta_p for which the reflected and refracted rays make an angle of 90 degrees between them is also called the Brewster angle theta_B; then tan theta_B = n holds.

blocks.alt: Top left: unpolarized light striking glass at the polarizing angle, the reflected ray marked as plane polarized and at 90 degrees to the refracted ray, with Brewster's law. Top right: a graph of transmitted intensity against angle following I0 cos squared theta, and the amplitude A0 split into A0 cos theta along the analyzer and A0 sin theta across it. Bottom left: polarized light rotated by an optically active sample before the analyzer. Bottom right: uses of polarization.
blocks.caption: Polarization by reflection, Brewster's law, Malus's law and optical activity (original diagram after Figures 8.6 to 8.8 and topics 8.4 and 8.5).
blocks.long_description: When unpolarized light meets glass at the polarizing angle, about 57 degrees, the reflected light vibrates only parallel to the surface and the reflected and refracted rays are at right angles, so the tangent of the polarizing angle equals the refractive index. A polarized wave reaching an analyzer at angle theta keeps only the part of its amplitude along the analyzer's axis, A0 cos theta, so the transmitted intensity is I0 cos squared theta: all of it at 0 degrees, none at 90 degrees. Optically active substances such as sugar solution turn the plane of polarization, by an amount set by the substance, its concentration, the path length and the wavelength.

blocks.text: Malus's law is also used to study the polarization of light in biological systems, such as the polarization of light by cell membranes (Interesting Information).

blocks.title: Example 8.1
blocks.text: A beam of light strikes the surface of a plate of glass with a refractive index of sqrt 3 at the polarizing angle. What will be the angle of refraction of the wave of light? Solution: n = sqrt 3, theta_r = ?. As tan theta_B = n, theta_B = tan^-1 (sqrt 3) = 60 degrees. As theta_r = 90 degrees - theta_B, theta_r = 90 degrees - 60 degrees = 30 degrees.

blocks.caption: Brewster angle relations
rows: n1 sin theta_p = n2 sin theta_r

blocks.prompt: We wish to use a glass plate of refractive index 1.5 in air as a polarizer; find the polarizing angle and the angle of refraction. At what angle of incidence will light reflected from water (n = 1.33) be completely polarized (numerical 8.7, 8.8)?
blocks.explanation: theta_p = tan^-1 1.5 = 56.3 degrees and theta_r = 90 - 56.3 = 33.7 degrees. For water theta_p = tan^-1 1.33 = 53 degrees.

items: Malus (1808): light reflected from glass is polarized; at about 57 degrees for glass it is plane polarized; light from a table top is partially polarized.

At the polarizing (Brewster) angle reflected and refracted rays are at 90 degrees: theta_p + theta_r = 90 degrees and tan theta_p = n2/n1 = n (from air). Example 8.1: n = sqrt 3, theta_B = 60 degrees, theta_r = 30 degrees.
